title: Control-plane migration led to tenant operator orphaning; surgical restart hotpatch & customer escalation playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: During a staged control-plane migration for multiple on-prem tenants, a timing window in the operator's leader-election + manifest reconcile logic allowed a subset of operator replicas to lose their tenant-scoped watches. Affected tenants showed 'degraded' in the Console, API requests were 503ing for ~12-45 minutes depending on tenant size. Multiple customers opened high-priority escalations. This ticket tracks the incident triage, a surgical restart hotpatch for stuck watchers, and follow-up reliability work.

Incident timeline: 
- 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC: Ops initiated control-plane migration (kube-apiserver upgrade + leader-election bump)
- 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC: First customer reports increased 5xx from inference endpoints
- 02:20-03:00 UTC: On-call confirmed operator controllers repeatedly attempted to rebind watches and hit a race with kubelet eviction events; operator metrics for 'watch_restarts' spiked
- 03:05 UTC: Emergency rollback aborted (would impact other tenants); team implemented a targeted 'surgical restart' of operator replicas for affected tenant namespaces which restored watches
- 04:00 UTC: Customers reporting recovery; Ops collection and postmortem started

Root cause hypothesis: Leader-election state transient combined with an internal reconcile path that assumed stable informers across replica restarts. Under control-plane churn some controllers dropped from the watch queue and failed to rebuild per-tenant caches because they skipped a code path (reconcile short-circuit) when mirror-secrets were present.

Mitigations applied: 
- Immediate: targeted restart of operator replica set in affected namespaces (hotpatch) using a selective rollout job to avoid global disruption
- Short term: added extra backoff and deterministic requeue on watch-failure path
- Monitoring: added a critical alert on 'operator.watch_stall_seconds' and a tenant-level degraded gauge

Customer communications: 
- Drafted joint incident update to customers at 2026-03-10T05:00Z with root cause summary and ETA for fix
- Support rep follow-ups scheduled with top 3 impacted accounts; credits and manual verification offered

Next steps/follow-ups tracked in this ticket: detailed in acceptance_criteria and comments below.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpatch rolled out and validated across 100% of affected tenants without introducing cascading restarts
New watch_stall metric firing correctly and routed to PagerDuty
Operator reconcile logic updated to avoid short-circuit on informer lapse and covered by unit+integration tests
Postmortem published with customer-facing timeline and remediation commitments
comments: 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - Liam Chen: Executed selective rollout script restart-operator-tenant.sh against namespaces: tenant-a, tenant-c, tenant-f. Watches recovered within 90s for small tenants, ~7m for large KV state tenants.
2026-03-10 04:05 UTC - Aisha Kumar: Customer communications sent. Top 3 customers accepted credit offer; engineering to validate no data loss in stateful caches.
2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - Priya Shah (SRE): Added prom rule operator_watch_stall_seconds > 30 -> p99; PagerDuty integration tested in staging
2026-03-12 16:45 UTC - Daniel Ortega (Eng): PR #2489 adds deterministic requeue and covers the reconcile short-circuit; needs integration test for informer restart
2026-03-13 10:05 UTC - Marta Ruiz (Solutions): Verified affected customers' post-fix telemetry and worked with Support to confirm endpoint success rates >99.9% for the last 24h
2026-03-14 11:00 UTC - Liam Chen: Deployed release operator-2026.03.14 to dedicated and private control planes; monitoring shows no regression after 48h
notes: Trade-offs considered: Global operator restart would be fastest to restore all watches but risked causing a larger outage; selective restart chosen to limit blast radius.
We avoided rolling back the control-plane upgrade because most tenants were healthy and rollback would require extended maintenance window.
